question: Why did the error rate go up on 10 March 2026?

contributing_factors.description: Upstream identity-db service is experiencing degraded performance, causing auth service errors.
why_chain: The error rate in auth service increased due to upstream identity-db service returning HTTP 503 errors.
The identity-db service is the upstream dependency of the auth service, and its degraded performance is causing the auth service to fail.
The identity-db service is experiencing timeout issues, leading to retries and eventually failing to respond within the auth service's timeout.

contributing_factors.description: The auth service is under higher load due to increased request volume.
why_chain: The error rate in auth service increased despite the request volume staying about the same.
The auth service is experiencing higher error rates despite the same request volume, indicating increased load.
The increased load on the auth service is causing it to fail more often, leading to higher error rates.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a configuration change in the auth service.
ruled_out.reason: The error rate increase is concentrated in the auth service, and the change point is specific to the auth service.

ruled_out.hypothesis: The increase in error rate is due to a data quality issue in the auth service.
ruled_out.reason: There is no evidence of unusual input data causing the error rate increase.

evidence.summary: Error rate for service auth rose from 0.39% to 5.84% (+1390%), with a change point at 2026-03-10T13:15:00Z.
The change is concentrated in service auth: 3 of 12 service/region segments changed; the other segments stayed flat (largest after/before ratio 1.33).
At the same time, request volume for service auth stayed about the same (1114 per 5 min before, 1326 per 5 min after, +19%).
At the same time, p95 latency for service auth rose (90 ms before, 163 ms after, +81%).
Upstream identity-db returning HTTP 503 for auth (auth; 1 min after the change; record R016)
auth: ERROR upstream identity-db timeout after 3 retries (auth, us-east; 12 min after the change; record R017)
auth: ERROR upstream identity-db timeout after 3 retries (auth, ap-south; 18 min after the change; record R018)
identity-db status page: investigating degraded performance (auth; 30 min after the change; record R020)
auth: ERROR upstream identity-db timeout after 3 retries (auth, eu-west; 22 min after the change; record R019)

reasons: ✓ A change event (alerts) lines up in time (1 min after the change).
✓ 4 log/alert record(s) after the change agree with the numbers.
✓ Request volume stayed steady, ruling out a traffic spike.
✓ No competing change event fits as well.
✓ The main factor rests on this event.

actions.action: Investigate and address the degraded performance of the identity-db service.
Monitor the identity-db service and implement retries or fallback mechanisms to handle transient failures.
Optimize the auth service to handle higher request volumes.
